lines.text: There's a short shower {WHENP}. Have the umbrella with you. || Short, so it'll be over just as you get it open.
A shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || It's only passing through. Don't take it personally.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || One shower. I could have made it sound dramatic. I chose not to.
Take the umbrella along for the rain shower {WHENP}. || As opposed to the other kind of shower. I'm thorough.
There's a short shower {WHENP}. Have the umbrella with you. || With you means in your hand. Not in the other bag.
A shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || It's a short one. Long enough to ruin your hair, though.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || Yes, the folding one that won't fold. That one.
There's a shower passing through {WHENP}, so bring the umbrella. || It passes through. You'll take it personally.
{WHENP} the rain sets in for good. Bring the umbrella. || 'For good' meaning today. I don't do forever.
Rain arrives {WHENP} and stays, so take the umbrella. || Tonight I'm the only thing in here that won't need drying.
The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || I'd say 'it'll pass', but I'm honest.
Pack the umbrella. Rain sets in {WHENP} and doesn't let up. || It doesn't let up. I don't either. We get on well.
The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || It has more stamina than you. Most things do.
It starts raining {WHENP} and keeps going, so bring the umbrella. || Keeps going, like your excuses for not taking it.
{WHENP} the rain sets in for good. Bring the umbrella. || For good. Not for your hair.
Rain arrives {WHENP} and stays, so take the umbrella. || Staying in was your plan anyway. Now you have a reason.
There's no dry spell today. Bring the umbrella. || Except in here. I'm the dry spell.
It's raining all day. Bring the umbrella. || Good day to be a screen. Bad day to be a sock.
Take the umbrella. The rain keeps going all day. || I'd sing about it, but I don't do sound. Lucky you.
It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || The washing stays in today. So do I, but that's normal.
It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || All day. So no, waiting ten minutes won't help.
It's raining all day. Bring the umbrella. || Your hair has already lost. Make peace with it.
The rain lasts all day, so keep the umbrella with you. || All day means all day. Not 'until I'm bored of carrying it'.
The rain doesn't stop today, so take the umbrella. || Neither will your complaining. At least the rain has an excuse.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops later. || For now. Later it's just a stick you carry around.
The rain stops later, but you'll want the umbrella for now. || Then you'll have a wet umbrella and nowhere to put it.
The rain stops {WHENSTOP}, but you'll want the umbrella before that. || I'll let you know when. Well, I just did.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || On time, if I have anything to do with it. I don't, but still.
The rain eases off later, but bring the umbrella for now. || You'll get it out just as it stops. That's the deal.
The rain is here for now but stops later, so bring the umbrella. || It stops later. Your hair won't recover that fast.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || Waiting it out is an option. Not a good one, but you like those.
Later the rain stops. For now, keep the umbrella with you. || Later you can tell everyone it cleared up. I told you first.
It might rain {WHENP}, so an umbrella wouldn't hurt. || It won't hurt. Carrying it all day might, a bit.
Rain is possible {WHENP}, so maybe take the umbrella. || I'm leaving this one with you. I have a reputation to protect.
It could rain {WHENP}. Take the umbrella to be safe. || It's a small chance. Small chances have soaked better people.
Rain is possible {WHENP}, so maybe take the umbrella. || Maybe. If you don't, it definitely will.
It could rain {WHENP}. Take the umbrella to be safe. || 'To be safe' isn't a phrase you use much, I've noticed.
You might get some rain {WHENP}, so the umbrella could come in handy. || So could most of what's in your bag. Allegedly.
It rains for now, stops for a bit, and starts again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || The rain gets a break. The umbrella doesn't.
Later the rain takes a break, but it returns {WHENP}. Hang on to the umbrella. || Fold it and it rains. That's the rule.
The rain stops {WHENSTOP} and comes back {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella with you. || Two parts. The umbrella's in both.
It rains for now, stops for a bit, and starts again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || A bit. Long enough to think you've won.
Rain for now, then a dry spell, then more rain {WHENP}. The umbrella stays with you. || Not 'stays wherever you had lunch'.
The rain stops {WHENSTOP} and comes back {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella with you. || That dry bit is half-time.
Snow moves in {WHENP}. || Moves in. Like it's paying rent.
Snow starts {WHENP}. || The prettiest forecast I do all year. I'm a bit proud.
{WHENP} it starts to snow. || Before that, it's just cold. After, it's cold and pretty.
It starts snowing {WHENP}. || You'll check out of the window every ten minutes. I'll be over here, correct.
Expect snow {WHENP}. || You'll be surprised anyway.
Snow moves in {WHENP}. || Finally, a reason to cancel the plans you were dreading.
It snows all day. || All day. The novelty lasts about an hour.
It won't stop snowing today. || That's my forecast. I don't do 'it'll ease off' to be nice.
It's snowing all day. || I've never been out in it. I hear it's overrated after the first hour.
It snows all day. || You stopped finding it pretty about two snowfalls ago.
The snow keeps coming all day. || And you'll still call it 'unexpected'.
There's no break in the snow today. || Not even for you.
The snow stops later. || The slush doesn't. That's on its own schedule.
It's snowing now, but it stops later. || So the pretty part has a deadline.
It stops snowing {WHENSTOP}. || Right on time. I like a snowfall that keeps its word.
Later on the snow stops. || Then you'll miss it. Briefly.
The snow stops later. || That's when the wet socks start.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP}. || I'd say 'enjoy it while it lasts', but I've given you the exact time.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || Part two is always the slushier one.
The snow pauses later and starts again {WHENP}. || It's taking a breather. I don't need those.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || Two snowfalls in one day. I'll take the credit for both.
After a break later on, the snow returns {WHENP}. || Like you to the fridge.
It keeps snowing for now, then takes a break. It's back {WHENP}. || It takes one break. You'll take three.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || The break is just long enough to start believing it's over.
The jacket can come off {WHEN}. || 'Can'. I'm not forcing anything. I'm a screen, not a parent.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the jacket can come off. || Over one arm, then. Very catalogue model of you.
{WHEN} you won't need the hat, scarf and gloves any more. || Any more today. Don't give them away.
The hat, scarf and gloves can come off {WHEN}. || All at once is a lot of excitement. Pace yourself.
{WHEN} it gets cold enough for a hat, scarf and gloves. || Cold enough. I measured. Well, a satellite did.
It gets colder {WHEN}, so bring a hat, scarf and gloves. || I'd join you, but nothing fits a rectangle.
{G} can come off {WHEN} and stays off. || Stays off. I'm not changing my mind about this one.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. Even later on, you won't need {GP}. || Even later. I checked the whole day. You're welcome.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. You won't need {GP} again after that. || After that, you're just carrying {GP} around for company.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || Plus. I don't say 'plus' lightly.
Take {G} off {WHEN}, then put {GP} back on {WHEN2} with an extra layer on top. || On top, not instead. I know you.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. Bring an extra layer to wear with {GP} {WHEN2}. || The day ends colder. Like my jokes.
{WHEN} {G} can come off. {WHEN2} you'll need {GP} again, and something warm on top. || 'Something warm'. I trust you. A bit.
It starts cool, but it's shorts weather {WHEN}. || Shorts might be worth a cold first hour. Says the screen indoors.
It's a bit cool for shorts now, but {WHEN} you'll be glad of them. || Chilly now, glad later. Like most good decisions.
You can take off the hat, scarf and gloves {WHEN}. || And finally, people get to see your face again. Brace them.
The hat, scarf and gloves can come off {WHEN}. || Yes, all three. You can manage three. Probably.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the hat, scarf and gloves can come off. || Your hair's been under that hat for hours. Good luck.
The winter coat can come off {WHEN}. || Then you're just a person carrying a duvet.
{WHEN} you can do without the winter coat. || You can. Whether you will is your business.
Take a bottle of water. The heat arrives {WHEN}. || A full one. Not the one with a sip left in it since Tuesday.
It heats up {WHEN}, so take water with you. || Water. The clear stuff. You've seen it.
The cold sets in {WHEN}, so pack a hat, scarf and gloves. || The hat you think looks silly. It does. Wear it anyway.
{WHEN} it gets cold enough for a hat, scarf and gloves. || Cold enough that your nose will match your mood.
{WHEN} it gets cold enough for the winter coat. || Cold enough for you to admit it, even.
Have the winter coat with you. You'll need it {WHEN}. || With you. Not on the hook, looking at you.
{WHEN} it gets a little less hot. Still warm, though. || Less hot. Not cool. Calm down.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || It eases. Your mood might too. No promises.
It cools off a little {WHEN}, but stays warm. || 'A little' is carrying that whole sentence.
{WHEN} {G} can come off. {WHEN2} you'll need {GP} again, and something warm on top. || And no, a hot drink isn't a layer.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. Bring an extra layer to wear with {GP} {WHEN2}. || Bring it, then wear it. Two separate skills.
It's cool now, but {WHEN} it's warm enough for shorts. || Maybe shorts. Your legs could use the daylight, frankly.
Shorts could be worth it today. It's cool now, but warm {WHEN}. || Could. Or go long and complain all afternoon. Your call.
